title: Request flow after the handler change
subtitle: How one Rust handler now returns an HTML fragment safely and predictably.

blocks.heading: The existing boundary
blocks.markdown: The browser sends a request to the **Rust handler**. The handler reads repository state and chooses a *response* with an inline `Content-Type` value. 1. Validate the request. 2. Persist the change. 3. Render the current state. - Full requests receive a document. - Enhanced requests receive a fragment. > Persisted state remains authoritative. | Request | Response | | --- | --- | | Full | Document | | Enhanced | Fragment | Read the [HTTP overview](https://example.com/http). Unsafe links stay inert: [script](javascript:alert(1)), [data](data:text/html,unsafe), and [VBScript](vbscript:msgbox(1)). Untrusted HTML stays text: & records.

right.title: Enhanced request
right.markdown: Returns the **changed fragment** with an inline `text/html` type.

blocks.title: Invariant
blocks.markdown: Both paths read the same persisted values before rendering. See the [request contract](https://example.com/contract).

blocks.heading: Follow the changed path
blocks.markdown:
1. **Validate:** reject an empty body before writing.
2. **Persist:** bind the body as a SQL value.
3. **Render:** read current rows and render the selected response.

blocks.caption: The persistence stage uses a dedicated code block

questions.question: Why does the handler re-read rows before rendering?
questions.markdown: The **database** is authoritative, so the response represents state *after* the write.

questions.question: What happens when a code language is unknown?
questions.markdown: The fallback preserves the source as inert `escaped text`.
